sources.entry: mFix - Open-source window manager with keyboard and drag snapping, snap layouts, a Cmd+Tab window switcher with live previews, and Dock window previews. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Zingzy/mFix) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: mFix is a free, open-source, native Swift window manager for macOS 26 that copies Windows 11 window management, including snapping, a window-level Cmd+Tab switcher, and Dock window previews.
summary.what_it_does: It snaps windows to halves, quarters and maximized states via keyboard shortcuts (Win is Cmd+Option by default) and by dragging to screen edges. It offers Windows 11-style Snap Layouts on hover of the green button, Snap Assist to fill empty space with other windows, and snap groups that resize together. Cmd+Tab is replaced by a window switcher with live thumbnails, and hovering a Dock icon shows that app's windows as cards. It adds Finder keys like Enter to open, Delete to trash, Cmd+X/Cmd+V to move files, and Cmd+L to go to a path. It also includes a Cmd+Option+Ctrl+T Always on Top pin, drag-and-drop previews, and a Win+D show-desktop shortcut.
use_cases: snap windows side by side on macOS
replace Cmd+Tab with a window switcher
keep a window always on top
cut and paste files in Finder
how_to_run: Or download mFix.dmg (requires macOS 26 Tahoe or later) and drag mFix into Applications
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/mFix.app (if macOS blocks the unsigned app)
Grant Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions when prompted
Build from source: swift build, swift test, scripts/build.sh, scripts/dmg.sh (requires Xcode 26)
notable: Windows 11 snap rules matched to a documented table, including quarters and multi-monitor moves
Snap groups and a divider handle that resizes adjacent snapped windows together
Cmd+Tab switcher shows windows rather than apps, with live thumbnails for on-screen windows
Always on Top implemented by overlaying a live copy of the pinned window, since macOS cannot raise another app's window
Native Swift with no Electron; the README cites a 583 KB download
caveats: Requires macOS 26 (Tahoe) or later; the README gives no support for older versions
Uses private macOS functions for minimized-window capture and window raising, which a macOS update could break
Not notarized, so macOS blocks the first launch and needs a manual bypass; ad hoc builds re-prompt for permissions on each rebuild
